consultas.metaDescription: Private medical consultations at Plenya — in person in Londrina or online via telemedicine, with Dr. Getúlio Amaral and the clinic's other physicians.
consultas.heroP: Health is not about reacting. It is about anticipating. The medical consultation at Plenya is where that medicine begins — long-form listening, careful reading of the data, and clear next steps even when labs come back "normal."
consultas.aboutP1: We make time to listen. A medical consultation at Plenya does not fit into fifteen minutes — and was not designed to. We review your history, your prior labs, your sleep, your routine, your body composition, and what has changed since someone last truly looked.
consultas.aboutP2: We work with a functional reading of labs: what is normal by laboratory reference and what is optimal from a clinical standpoint are rarely the same thing. When indicated, we order additional tests and build a plan — medication, lifestyle adjustment, referral to the multidisciplinary team, or all of them together.
consultas.aboutP3Part1: Every Plenya Consultation delivers an honest reading of your data, a clear plan, and what needs to start now — it can stand alone or repeat in your own time, as your health requires. When care needs continuity — a team following alongside, a single plan, and cycle-based reviews — the next step is called
consultas.modalitiesText: In person at our clinic in Londrina (PR, Brazil), or online via telemedicine — with the same clinical depth.

consultas.doctorsDesc: Every physician at Plenya was chosen for alignment with the same medicine — rigorous, anticipatory clinical work integrated with the multidisciplinary team. You can choose which professional you'd like to see.
consultas.otherDoctorsDesc: Physicians trained in different specialties, all anchored in integrative functional medicine and The ACTS Method. They work alongside the multidisciplinary team — nutritionist, psychologist, and exercise physiologist — so every therapeutic plan is built in coordination.

consultas.faqTitle: Questions we hear every week about the Plenya Consultation.
consultas.faq1Q: How long does a Plenya Consultation last?
consultas.faq1A: On average 60 to 90 minutes for the first visit — the time needed to review history, prior labs, and build a plan. Follow-up visits typically run 45 to 60 minutes.
consultas.faq2A: Both — your choice. In person at our clinic in Londrina, Brazil, or online via telemedicine, with the same clinical depth.
consultas.faq3A: No. We see patients on a private-pay basis only. In Brazil, medical expenses are tax-deductible as health spending under current law.
consultas.faq4A: Yes, whenever possible. The more history we have, the better the reading — laboratory tests, imaging, prior reports, and current medications.
consultas.faq5Q: Does the consultation include ordering new labs?
consultas.faq5A: Yes, when clinically indicated. The order is yours to take to the lab of your choice.
consultas.faq6Q: What is the difference between a Plenya Consultation and Continuum Plenya?
consultas.faq6A: The Consultation addresses a moment. The Continuum builds a trajectory — multidisciplinary team following alongside, a single plan, and re-evaluations on a 6- or 12-month cycle.

drGetulio.metaTitle: Dr. Getúlio Amaral Filho — Clinical Director
drGetulio.metaDescription: Brazilian physician, nephrologist, and specialist in integrative functional medicine. Clinical director of Plenya.
drGetulio.heroP1: Brazilian physician trained at the State University of Londrina (UEL) in 2004. Board-certified in nephrology and internal medicine through Santa Casa de Londrina, with formal certification from the Brazilian Society of Nephrology. He coordinates the nephrology residency at Santa Casa and serves as medical director of DaVita Intra Hospitalar de Londrina.
drGetulio.heroP2: His postgraduate training in integrative functional medicine through ABMFI underpins Plenya's positioning: the same clinical rigor of the hospital setting, applied years before the diagnosis takes hold.
drGetulio.aboutP1: Over two decades in internal medicine and nephrology, with much of that work conducted within the hospital setting. Daily practice meant following patients in advanced stages of kidney and cardiovascular disease — cases in which, often, the trajectory could have been changed years earlier, through routine decisions and more careful monitoring.
drGetulio.aboutP2: Integrative functional medicine is not an alternative to conventional medicine. It is a way of organizing preventive care with the same rigor applied to hospital care — labs, data, structured decision-making — directed at what precedes disease.
drGetulio.aboutP3: That is the medicine I lead at Plenya, alongside the team that came together for this purpose.

about.metaTitle: About Plenya — Manifesto, Purpose, and Method
about.metaDescription: Discover the manifesto, the purpose, and The ACTS Method behind Plenya. Integrative functional health, continuous and personalized.
about.manifesto3: Living well is the reflection of what you choose every day.
about.manifesto4: It is awareness. It is freedom.
about.originP1Part1: Plenya was born from the passion of
about.originP1Part2: and the team that came together around him — physicians, nutritionist, psychologist, and exercise physiologist — for life in its full form and for longevity lived with clarity, energy, and purpose.
about.originP2: Across more than two decades between hospital wards, dialysis units, and the consulting office, Dr. Getúlio watched medicine save lives in critical conditions — and saw, in parallel, people living longer and living worse, fragmented across five or six clinicians who never spoke to one another. Patients with "normal" labs who were already falling ill in silence.
about.originP3Part1: Plenya is the clinical answer to that observation. A model designed to see earlier, follow closely, and act with clarity — focused on
about.originP4: Because living longer is no longer enough. What matters is how you live.
about.clinicCaption: Architectural render of the future Plenya headquarters. Reception and environment designed for hospitality and continuous care.
about.teamCaption: Physicians, nutritionist, psychologist, and exercise physiologist — a single team that meets, discusses the case, and designs an integrated plan of care.
about.purposeTitle: To guide people toward living longer and better, with autonomy over their own health.
about.purposeP1: In a landscape shaped by information overload and fragmented approaches, Plenya offers care that is integrated, personalized, and sustainable over time. We connect different areas of health into a single structured plan — built on data, proximity, and shared responsibility.
about.goldenTitle: Why we exist. How we care. What we deliver.
about.goldenWhy: Because people are living longer, but not necessarily better — and they continue to be treated in parts, not as a whole. No one should arrive at the most important phase of life limited by the choices made before.
about.goldenHow: Through integrated, continuous, and personalized care that connects different areas of health into a single structured plan — with data, proximity, and shared responsibility.
about.goldenWhat: A health and longevity program that combines a multidisciplinary team, a proprietary method (ACTS), and close follow-up to transform habits, body, and mind in a sustainable way.
about.agirSectionTitle: Four interdependent pillars for health that sustains over time.
about.agirSectionDesc: The clinical framework that organizes Plenya's care. It is not a protocol — it is a way of structuring medical follow-up around what sustains health over the long term.
about.agirSectionCta: Discover The ACTS Method in full
about.positioningTitle: Fragmented care is the problem. Integration is the answer.
about.positioningDesc: Today, the patient moves between different clinicians, sources of information, and conflicting advice — with no clarity, no continuity, and no single direction. At Plenya, we integrate clinical work, data, and close follow-up to turn care into a continuous, personalized, and measurable process.

method.metaDescription: The ACTS Method organizes Plenya's clinical care into four interdependent pillars — Activity, Alimentation & Smart Adjuncts; Clinical Optimization; Tending Mind, Body & Bonds; Sleep, Rhythm & Recovery. Anticipatory medicine with depth.
method.heroTitle: ACTS — four pillars for health that sustains over time.
method.heroSubtitle: Plenya's clinical framework organizes care into four interdependent dimensions of health. It is not a protocol. It is the way we decide, monitor, and follow up — with the depth that longevity demands.
method.premiseTitle: The body does not wait for the diagnosis to fall ill.
method.premiseP1: By the time blood sugar climbs, insulin resistance has been building for a decade. By the time a heart attack happens, the plaque has been growing for twenty years. The window for intervention exists — but it closes in silence.
method.premiseP2: The ACTS Method is how we operate inside that window. Four interdependent pillars that, together, organize preventive care with the same rigor applied in hospital medicine — labs, data, structured decisions — directed at what comes before disease.
method.monitoredFootnote: Partial list — actual monitoring covers dozens of additional markers per pillar, tailored to your case.
method.convictionsTitle: Five sentences that took a decade to become convictions.
method.applyTitle: Applied by a team. Measured by the Plenya Score.
method.applyP1: The ACTS Method is the framework that organizes our clinical decisions and our communication with you. The Plenya Score translates your current state into a number that evolves throughout follow-up — so progress is clear, measurable, and shared.
method.applyP2: The rule of two operates here: we begin with two focuses, with clinical judgment, and advance at the pace of your body — not at the pace of well-meaning lists.
method.p1Territory: The three engines no medication can replace
method.p1Intro: Food is not fuel — it is information. Every meal instructs genes, modulates hormones, and feeds the microbiome. Exercise is the most powerful medication available. Supplementation corrects what the lab shows is missing. The three engines work together.
method.p1Quote: Medication takes care of what it reaches. The rest — insulin, inflammation, sarcopenia, microbiome — depends on what you do every day.
method.p1M4: Vitamin D, B12, iron, and omega-3 status
method.p2Intro: Hormones, biomarkers, data-guided pharmacology. The part of the work where the physician stops being a lifestyle counselor and becomes the pilot of a data dashboard — test, intervene, retest, adjust.
method.p2Quote: Ordering TSH alone is like checking the faucet pressure without verifying that water is coming out. Metabolic management begins by ordering the right test.
method.p2M1: Full hormone panel (free testosterone, SHBG, estradiol, DHEA-S, cortisol, thyroid)
method.p2M2: ApoB, lipoprotein(a), CAC score when indicated
method.p2M5: Genetic markers when indicated — precision medicine
method.p3Intro: The axis between psychology, the immune system, and inflammation. Psychological states directly alter immune, hormonal, and inflammatory function — not as metaphor, as mechanism. When the HPA axis is on chronic alert, no other pillar functions fully.
method.p3Quote: Ana optimized everything biochemistry would allow. The hs-CRP would not come down. What needed treatment was the anxiety she called personality.
method.p3M5: Quality of relationships and social support
method.p4Territory: The substrate on which the other pillars operate
method.p4Intro: Sleep, chronobiology, the synchronization of biological clocks. The suprachiasmatic nucleus is the conductor; every cell has its clock. When signals arrive at unpredictable times, the orchestra goes out of tune — and the name for that is chronodisruption.
method.p4Quote: When the substrate is compromised, everything built above starts to crack. Sleep is not a pillar like the others — it is the base.
method.p4M2: Symptoms and screening for obstructive sleep apnea
method.c1Text: The body does not wait for the diagnosis to fall ill.
method.c1Sub: Disease begins ten, fifteen, twenty years before the label. The window for intervention exists — but it closes. And it closes in silence.
method.c2Text: No one changes everything at once.
method.c2Sub: Two focuses per quarter, with measure and deadline. Those who try to change ten things on Monday usually have changed none by Friday.
method.c3Text: The pillars do not work in isolation.
method.c3Sub: Nutrition without sleep is wear-down. Exercise without recovery is overtraining. Hormones without mental health is optimization on sand.
method.c4Sub: No patient does it alone. Preventive medicine is networked work — physician, multidisciplinary team, and the patient at the center.
method.c5Text: The best time to start was ten years ago. The second-best time is today.
method.c5Sub: This is not a motivational line. It is clinical data. Reversibility decreases over time. The cost of inaction increases with age.
